Actually, I've been wondering that too Lord Fyr, I do not mean to accuse, but, what were you doing down there?
You don't think you're the only ones with a stake in all this do you?
The Clockwork City was as much a product of my drunken tirades as it was Sotha Sil's!
Perhaps not my home, but I have as much of a duty to protect it as you do.
Then please, Lord Fyr, do you have any idea what would cause the catacombs to assault us? We've done nothing out of the ordinary. For fabricants, at least.
That's actually precisely what we're investigating. But, we're mostly unsure.
Reactionary plating analysis helped, bit archaic how Sotha Sil built his machines, but it is easy to recognize tampering on pliactic surfaces.
Uh. Lord Fyr, can you perhaps, translate what Lord Bagarn said?
He said that someone has been sabotaging your little dig.
That shouldn't have happened! I mean that really should not have happened. Nobody, especially the Thalmor, know we are down here.
Unless someone told them.
The saboteur? Lord Fyr, please tell me you have something on that.
Not me, but Yagrum did discover something.
Mechanical tracings are conclusive.  Whoever lead them here came in through your backdoor, and set things up prior to our arrival.
But, does not carry fabricant signatures.
What are you saying?
Your traitor is an outsider, someone with access to your mine, who arrived recently. And there's only one person here who fits that description.
Hmph, I should be the Century in charge of Lull-Mor, not Numinar. I've done more for the Clockwork City than every fool here.
I played for the Cacophany, was secretary to the High Foremer, there's even a helicarrier named after me!
But what does achieving things in life get you? A drunken lout of a husband, and court-marshalled just because I ripped his skull out!
What? No, of course not, did you never pay attention as a child? You can't kill a fabricant with something as low-key as that!
He's over there, on the table. Grumbles a lot, but his eye sockets can hold things for me. Finally makes himself useful.
I don't care what you're here for, go away!
Ever since that mining team came I've had to deal with the most inane requests that would be best put to someone else! And I am sick of it!
You want to use the Upgate, fine. But if you're not actually here on important business, then you'll do it yourself.
I'm sick of getting requests to make the Upgate take someone to somewhere that isn't an essential part of my work.
I've made modifications so that you and your friends can all operate the gate of your own accord, and go off and do whatever things you kids do.
Here's the instruction manual and the tools you need to set a destination. Now if you need anything, please, go ask someone else.

Nasty stuff those undead. Still, the stress helps with inspiration. Have a look at this new harquebus I sketched up.
Ah, hello outsider, didn't they arrest you? Ah well, we live and learn. If you're off to the Cave, maybe you could try out this harquebus?
That shield of yours is interesting. Here, I might be able to do something with it, if you could provide me with some extra materials.
Hey.
I heard that you had arrived. It is good to finally meet you, Dragonborn.
Is it really so surprising to think that you are the only person to be invited down here? We all have our parts to play, after all.
My name is Medeliu Hammar, of House Telvanni.
And please, let us just get this out of the way, I do in fact, know everything.
You will find, Dragonborn, that the passions of power fade with time.
Mage duels and scheming lose their edge with the centuries, and one finds pleasure in dedicating themselves to the simpler things.
For me, I'd rather have my books, my tower, and my... adequate children.
In my old age, I focus not on spells, but on words, and through the years I have amassed quite literally the whole of all knowledge in existence.
It's something of a source of pride for me.
In many ways yes. If you reach a point in your travels when you are stuck, come to me for advice, and I may help you.
In the meantime, I can always give you a little primer on the deeper aspects of the world.
No spoilers though. It is always best if you figure things out yourself.
Understand the Dwemer saw creation as a prison, a cage that robbed them of their immortal forms.
The Altmer believed as such, but the Dwemer dedicated their existence to this belief, as well as the desire to break free of it.
They eventually proposed a god of their own, a machine called Numidium, which would break apart the world, and free them of their mortal coil.
And that is it, Dragonborn. The Dwemer, in their final moments, merged with their Brass God, becoming its final components.
It is not a complicated thing, what happened to them. They are simply something else, and something far more dangerous.
Under the guide of a Shezarrine, Numidium could be controlled, but let loose, it is a greater threat than anything Nirn will ever know.
The collective souls of an entire race of furious world-deniers in the body of an enormous brass golem would spell disaster for the world.
Only a fool would want them back.
They are artifical and sometimes natural creations, constructs that keep the world stable. If Nirn is a song, the Towers compose its symphony.
Now, each Tower has a focal point, a Stone, as it is called, that keeps it active.
These Stones can range from small objects to complicated constructs, but they can be used and, unfortunately, destroyed.
If a Stone is destroyed, that Tower is considered deactivated. That is, it no longer keeps the world stable.
The more Towers that go down, the more unstable the world becomes.
The Chronographers understandably have a vested interest in keeping such Towers active, for what good it does them...
Many, many Towers have been deactivated already. White-Gold Tower, Red Mountain, Walk-Brass, Crystal-Like-Law, Orichalc, Green-Sap, all dead.
Of the many Towers, only Snow-Throat, the Throat of the World, and Ada-Mantia, that which you call Direnni Tower, remain active.
Well, that is a bit of a complicated question. To be exact, you are still on Nirn, and still, logically speaking, in Skyrim.
Or rather, you are underneath. Deep underneath, in fact. We are technically on the outskirts of the Clockwork City of Sotha Sil.
They refer to this place as Lull-Mor.
One of the three original Tribunal, mortals who stole godhood.
Sotha Sil was perhaps unique among them, a reclusive mystic who hid himself away in the depths of the world.
He created what you see before you, as well as the fabricants you have spoken to.
Remember, you'll be deep in Thalmor territory. That disguise you have might just be the only thing keeping you alive, so keep it on!
I can also tell you that combat will not help you much. Instead, try a stealth approach.
The enemies in there will be not your concern. Rather, you must take care to avoid obstacles.
The Boiling Foundry is still active, and you might often fall to your death. Talk to Avarri on that matter, he might have something for you.
Fabricant Undead are much different than the undead you have faced before.
If you find yourself unable to hurt one, simply flee until a better opportunity presents itself.
Archeron's creations are, though I hesitate to use the word, invincible.
They cannot be killed by normal means, rather, you must use your shield to knock them into the lifeblood of the world, unmaking them.
I recommend you carry all the tools you've acquired in your quest so far, you will be in the very heart of the Wheels of Lull after all.
Good to see you again, Dovahkiin.
Your presence honors us. Please, speak freely.
Make it quick, outlander.
You are not Mzark.
Oh well, excuse me for trying to relate! I suppose if you're going to be anti-social, fine. We'll skip the introductions.
Now, what do you want?
Yet I do mortal! I am the Cartwright, Lord of the Rails, the Blastdoors, the Lifts, and... oh, what's the point?
I ran all the transportation in Sotha Sil, but... but now everyone is off on their own, and no transportation is used!
Now I'm sitting here all alone, trying to entertain some idiot adventurer who isn't even impressed when I reference their past adventures!
So what's the point of being a noncorporeal machine if you can't go anywhere and nobody is impressed?
Ohhhh interests. Must be nice having something to do, eh? I bet you just LOVE killing Draugr. Wish I could kill Draugr. I wish I knew what a Draugr w
No, it would be boring. I could destroy you, upload your mind into a machine, and perhaps then we could entertain each other.
After all, you are an intruder on MY tramway. I have a sacred duty to destroy you.
Well, not much I actually know about interests, being me. I suppose I've... I've always liked riddles, I guess.
Perhaps that would be nice. Very well, mortal, here's how it will go. If you solve my riddles, I'll advance the tram for you.
If not, well, you die. Simple, and fun. Shall we begin?
What goes in the water black and comes out red?
What ends everything always?
What asks but never answers?
Oh, I'm sorry, I'm afraid that's incorrect. And by I'm sorry, I mean I'm going to kill you now.
Wrong! Goodbye!
Do you like it? It's a little tune I wrote for when you're correct.
Not bad, I'll advance things forward now.
Dragonborn, a moment please, I'm afraid there's something I need you to do.
Not me, so much as Lull-Mor itself.
Team Four are nice people, but unfortunately pay little attention to the failing mechanisms of their town.
The machines that keep the town operating are starting to fail. Don't worry, they simply need a bit of tweaking. This is what I need you for.
Use these two tools on the monitors around Lull-Mor to diagnose and repair any problems you find.
The diagnosing tool will tell you the problem if there is one, and the repair tool will fix it, provided you use them correctly.
And I appreciate your help.
You would eventually anyway, so as far as I understand it, you've said yes.
And I know you have. Now, wasn't that a fun little distraction?
No? Yes? Does it really matter? It had to be done, might as well be you who does it. Again, I thank you for your help.
Oh, as for a reward, here. This book was a favorite of my son's when he was a child, though one can only wonder why. It's a bit of a disturbing tale.
Pssst, kid! Hey, kid. Shamble over here a sec, got something to ask you.
What do you mean, dead? Look, outsider, I know you folks eat trees or whatever, but you're mortal, same as us!
Ain't nobody dying just because their wife ripped out their skull, that's just ridiculous!
It ain't being a skull that's all the problem, see, it's the missus over there having the mind to deny me.
Water, kid, I'm talking about water! There's oily stuff all around here, but I'm talking about the good stuff.
Fresh spring water, hot water, raindrops if you're feeling in an exotic mood.
And here we are sitting right below it, and she's all saying that she wants me sober! Pff, never did anything good sober.
Just a bottle of it, kid. Fresh, cold, hot, I don't care, just as long as you get me some.
Now listen, took me years to get this on account of having no arms, but I got this water bottle.
Just equip it or whatever you do while in some water, it'll fill right up.
You bring that to me, and I got something real good that I can give you in return.
And not a word of this to the wife, y'hear? I don't wanna lose that water bottle.
Ungrateful, lazy s'wit!
I thought he had learned his lesson. I even let him have a glass of some of the oiled lubricant we keep about, and this is how he repays me!
Thank you, dear, it is nice to see honesty is still alive, even if it's in unexpected places.
But I don't think simply taking away this water bottle will help. Oh no, punishment must be rendered.
Take this bottle to Lord Hammar, in the library, and tell him you need a potion of guilt.
He'll mix one up in this bottle, and when my husband takes a sip, he'll learn that it does no good to go behind someone's back!
Haha, knew I was throwing my lot in with the right guy. Give it here.
(The Skull drinks the water.)
Oh yessh, that right there thins out the mechanismshs. You held up your bargain of the end all nice and good-like, here, let me give you something.
Wife kept this little trinket hidden in my mouth, don't think she'll mind if it goes missing for a good cause.
Smells a bit funny. You fill it up with one of them hot spring waters? Ah, whatever, give it here!
(The Skull drinks the potion.)
Oh. Ohhh gods. What did you fill this with, kid? I feel like my arms on fire. I don't have arms! You talked to that wife of mine, didn't you?
Well the deal's off! I'll keep this for myself now... just. Ugggh, I don't feel good.
Ah, I think I know where you're going with this. It's not a potion so much as a mild poison, specifically for fabricants.
The actual mechanisms of its workings are more complex than that, but I can make you one easily enough.
I'll need you to bring me two snowberries, a daedra heart, and scrounge up a pneuma from around the town.
What do you mean, what's with him? Have you never seen a Dwemer before?
Oh, don't gawp. But that's a question you'd better ask the mer himself.
I am Divayth Fyr, formerly of Great House Telvanni, and greatest wizard east of Alinor. This is no boast, but a simple statement of fact.
In a word? Enigmatic. I had the privilege of being the closest mortal to him, yet I confess that his intellect confounded even my own at times.
He was compassionate, in his own way, but poor at showing it and slow to act, and as the centuries wore on he became increasingly insular.
I don't know for sure. I was exploring the Outer Realms during the battle of Red Mountain.
When I returned, my kin were vanished and the Blight had descended upon Resdayn.
I have my ideas, of course, but I haven't yet hit upon incontrovertible proof of them.
Whenever I get a chance to visit the Clockwork City, even in its sadly diminished state, I leap to do so.
Even now, it's a beautiful realm, wouldn't you say? Ah, but you should have seen it in its heyday - it was magnificent.
You have a purpose, a point! Bad things are afoot Dovahkiin, you have to fix them!
We do not go mad, not us! We break, our mechanisms in our head twist and turn! It is madness of a sort, but no prince rules it!
And it is with a capital B please, Broken, not broken.
Was the trolley station! Went places, don't really know where never used it! But broken now. Might not be, if you get the hint.
Not much, can't. Not at all. Nope. Clean the floors, clean the chairs, clean the tables. Don't stack them though, I'm not an ash slave.
Shhhhhhh, it's a secret.
Know your equipment I do, need help? I can tell you what it does, yes I can!
Lets you see what I see! Lullian mechanics, see them, change the world!
Though you might be able to see them a bit already, little wiggles in the world. Wiggles, fun word that.
Not a staff, a rod! Rod. Rod. Charges up old mechanisms, things that lack the power of the earth! Brings them back to life, what life they have.
Shoot it at a blue spike, watch something happen!
Goveri's unwinder! Built for fighting fabricant undead. Swing it hard, out comes the unwindings!
Not much use there nowadays though, but it can suspend working mechanisms and let you access things you couldn't before. Very useful.
See a green slash, slash at the green slash, access a cache.
I'm afraid I'm a bit absorbed in work right now, don't worry though, there will be plenty of time for talk later.
Of course Talos is a god. The question is, is Talos a man? For starters, Talos is not a single person, but a collection of Shezarrines.
Though the god of space, Lorkhan, is dead, he manifests through avatars, incarnations of himself we call "Shezarrines", taken from his Imperial name.
Talos is, in fact, merely part of the Oversoul of Lorkhan.
And Lorkhan is perhaps one of the most powerful entities in existence, if not the most powerful.
Talos is surely a god, but given his status as Lorkhan, it is hard to say that he was ever a man.
Well, in some ways you are already! You are Dragonborn, part of a figment of the Akatoshian Oversoul, much like your fellow dragons and Alduin.
You are, in many ways, immortal, though having part of the soul of an insane god is not something I'd envy.
How do I explain this... Most gods and Daedra are simply smaller subgradients of a greater being.
Dragons are smaller parts of Akatosh. This is how you absorb their souls - you are simply merging existing pieces of yourself with yourself.
Brhuce? Yes, I believe he's been wandering the world. I apologize for his behavior, he was always an odd child, even before his obsessions began.
There were many iterations of the world that Magnus designed. Some well known, like Hermaeus Mora, or Sybandis, others less so.
Eventually, they settled on the design you see today.
Put simply, the Wheels are the literal clockwork that drives the world, its underlying mechanisms that make the sun rise and the weather change.
It was first proposed by Lorkhan, designed by Magnus, and later discovered by Sotha Sil, who took control of it and made the Clockwork City.
I'm afraid that I'd rather not say. Partially because I promised him not to tell, partially because I'd rather let you figure it out by yourself.
See? Much better. Take a fabricant, stop his time, if his pneuma's intact, he'll be fine!
Just the real me here, just the pneuma! Easier this way, no waiting up for me, no me getting stuck in walls. That happens a lot for some reason. Heh!
But we're wasting time really! Go to Stonehole Mine! Little place, near Dawnstar, old, abandoned, Third Era, very nice.
Southwest of Dawnstar, go!
Forgot to mention, it's haunted. Very haunted.
That's everywhere in Skyrim though, makes you wonder what's so good if the spirits keep sticking around. Hahaha!
They dug too deep they did, too far, found my home, found the Wheels of Lull, and drove them mad it did!
Mad enough to have quite a few tricks up their sleeve! Careful!
Killed each other, miner turning on miner, and so lie here, still mad, still dead, one big happy crazy dead family.
Useful though, we use them to guard the place. Sotha Sil shouldn't be easy to reach after all.
Lull-Mor, Skyrim outpost of Sotha Sil, Chronographer Station Number 4, Snow-Throat monitor! Not working!
Disrepair, things are going wrong at the Top of the World and we feel it at the bottom! Why? Boss Numinar wants to know!
Talk to him, at the center tower! If you'll excuse poor little me, I have a new body to find. Off I roll!
How is not obvious to you that something called an Upgate can create gates up to the surface?
It was named that so people wouldn't ask stupid questions like that. Of course, it can do more than just return you to the surface.
If I'm not busy, which I will be, I can set it to take someone to a variety of locations.
If you ask nicely some time, perhaps I will show you a demonstration.
Ohhh I know about Llavados alright.
Numinar brought him with to clean up the place, but half the time I find him poking around in mechanisms that he shouldn't!
I don't trust that little man now, he talks like he's crazy but acts much differently. Watch yourself around him.
There used to be hundreds of these outposts. They call them towns now, but in the height of the Clockwork City every great pillar had a team.
Of course, the idiots didn't bother to keep things running, so now only Lull-Mor remains.
The little gold bugs that beep? I hope you aren't harassing them outsider!
Those are Formation Repair Fabricants, or FRFs, and they do nothing but help us! If they're bothering you, then good, they have a reason to do so.
Yes, maybe that will put him off the drink for a while. Fool thinks he can go behind my back, and look where it gets him.
Now, here, dear, I'm sure this little trinket will come in handy.
That's a Watchman. In the Clockwork City, they were our guards, but they haven't worked for a while.
I've been trying to restore him, to give the place more security.
I tend to avoid him. You should too.
I'm the Century. As highest ranking Chronographer I keep everyone in line and keep our Tower operating. Not the best job, but... eh.
Broken, like the rest of them. Good smith though. He'd be able to explain his condition better than I can.
It's a cutting sphere. A Dwemer creation. Round, yet sharp. It's my only trophy these days, for what little comfort it actually brings...
I shouldn't indulge myself, but... it has been such a long time. Perhaps a trade?
I've studied this cutting sphere for centuries now, it's a useful weapon, but I'd gladly exchange it for your harquebus.
It... will be nice to experiment again.
Oh. Okay.
I suppose you are right. Perhaps I am just bitter, so many of us were downgraded when the Clockwork King died. I shall collect your data.
In my youth, I was a bit more accepting. I liked new things, and I was curious. I once broke into the Watchmen headquarters dressed as one of them.
Now, I don't like new things. New things mean trouble. Trouble is dealt with accordingly.
My lord, I present a new arrival to you.
Ah, my lord, I must protest, our guest comes from Elenwen's entourage, apparently they were a bit too friendly with the cook!
My fault, my lord, I had yet to give you the message, I was busy at the gate, as you know.
My lord?
Yes my lord, thank you my lord.
I wasn't informed of any new arrivals. Kill them.
And yet, I wasn't informed of this.
Then you are excused, Secarius.
You have failed to inform me of an essential message. Not entirely your fault, I admit, so I will be easy. I think an hour on the rack will be good.
Toodle-loo, I'm here to save you!
All right, you lot, listen up! You all know why we're here!
Maybe some of us said the wrong thing, or did the wrong thing, or were just too mad, even for a fabricant.
But as Broken, homicidal, and mad as we are, we are still Chronographers! Sons of Seht, Timekeepers, Memonurses!
And we do our job. Now is the time to prove that!
A Thalmor agent, a mystic who stole the knowledge of our god has learned of that which we keep hidden, the Stone of Snow-Throat.
He will reach it, and he will use it, and he will destroy it! He insults us, he thinks that no one will get in his way, but I tell you, he's wrong!
When he steps into that Cave at the bottom of the mountain, he'll find a crew of angry fabricants waiting!
My fellows, we are going to drill to Snow-Throat's underworks, and beat this foul Altmer to the Stone!
